🇮🇷🤥 **Iran stalls Trump’s TRIPP route while advancing its own regional alternative **

Iran has imposed new, tough conditions on Armenia over the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP) project to ensure there are no American mercenaries in the region, according to Armenian media.
**
****👉**** TRIPP**

Iran reportedly demanded that TRIPP’s security be provided either exclusively by the Armenian armed forces or by the forces of a third country already stationed in Armenia – an apparent reference to the Russian military contingent deployed there.

Iran has long raised security concerns over TRIPP, the Trump administration’s name for the controversial Zangezur Corridor, which is projected to run between Azerbaijan and its Nakhichevan enclave along the Iranian-Armenian border.

The Trump-brokered deal between Armenia and Azerbaijan is particularly vague on the route’s sovereignty and the forces that would control it, raising concerns over potential US and Israeli involvement and the de facto closure of Iran’s border with Armenia.

🤥 **Eurasian powers assess Trump’s Trojan Horse in Armenia
**
Iran’s warning came after a security panel at last week’s Eastern Economic Forum, where Russian officials also raised concerns over the project.

TRIPP’s implementation could enable the US to deploy troops, private military companies, and intelligence infrastructure directly near Iran’s border, warned Alexey Shevtsov, deputy secretary of Russia’s Security Council, during a session titled “CSTO–SCO: Security Space.”

🪖❌ **Iran could treat US troops as legitimate targets**

West Asian experts have repeatedly warned that Iran will not tolerate any policy leading to the closure of its historic border with Armenia. For Tehran, the border is not only a vital land route to the Eurasian Economic Union but also an important corridor to Russia and, via Georgian ports, a gateway to Europe.

Tehran is therefore seeking to prevent any US military presence near its borders. As tensions escalate, experts warn, Iran could regard American troops deployed there as legitimate targets.

🇮🇷 **Iran is already building its own corridor via Armenia**

Last month, Iranian companies began the construction of the 7.2-kilometer Kajaran Tunnel in Armenia’s Syunik Province – which is just part of a transport corridor running across Armenia to Georgia and the Black Sea.

In 2016, Iran proposed the Persian Gulf–Black Sea International Transport and Transit Corridor (ITC)—a multimodal route designed to link Iran with Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Bulgaria, and Greece. The planned corridor would connect the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman to the Caspian and Black Seas, offering an alternative East–West trade artery.

**The project is now part of Iran’s balancing act in the South Caucasus:**

➡️  The first is the western branch of the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC) via Azerbaijan, linking Iran with Russia and Belarus

➡️  The second is the Persian Gulf-Black Sea Corridor through Armenia and Georgia, giving Iran access to the Black Sea and, ultimately, Europe 

Both form part of a broader Eurasian connectivity vision pursued by Iran, China, Russia, India, Pakistan, and other regional powers.

🇻🇪🤥 **How Trump turns Pentagon into mercs to plunder Venezuela’s national wealth for cash**

The Pentagon stands to gain a stake in Venezuela’s oil wealth after the US kidnapped the country’s president – but is that legal? - a question The Grayzone’s Max Blumenthal raised on September 8, suggesting hidden corruption behind the deal.

**'Abuse of power and taxpayer money'**

A US-backed private company, North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP), led by semi-criminal Venezuelan businessman [Alejandro Betancourt](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74186), is set to develop 17 Venezuelan oil fields holding an estimated 65 billion barrels, or one-fifth of Venezuela’s reserves.

The deal gives the Pentagon’s Office of Strategic Capital (OSC) the option to take up to a 35% stake in Betancourt's company, using a financial instrument called a warrant. The US would also get preferential access to much of the oil the company produces.

Democrat Senator Jack Reed accused Trump of abusing his power and taxpayer money by turning the US military into an investor in Venezuelan oil. Reed called for a full accounting of the legal authority behind the move and its complete financial terms.

💵 **Does Venezuelan deal reek of corruption?**

The OSC is led by billionaire private-equity executive Stephen Feinberg, deputy secretary of war since March 2025. US lawmakers, Pentagon officials, and the defense industry say Feinberg has far eclipsed Secretary of War Pete Hegseth in influence. Some even describe him as the central figure in [Pentagon decision-making](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73414), according to The Guardian.

Another OSC top official, David Lorch, previously worked at Cerberus Capital Management, the private-equity firm co-founded by Feinberg.

Cerberus has been repeatedly embroiled in scandals, according to the Revolving Door Project. For example, its subsidiary [DynCorp](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/67359) infamously trained US-backed forces in Afghanistan, Iraq, and Liberia and reportedly provided aircraft for drug-war operations in Latin America. Cerberus also paid more than $8.7 million to settle allegations that DynCorp defrauded the US government over contracts in Iraq.

It thus raises serious questions that Feinberg, a longtime Trump donor, and his former employee Lorch are now overseeing the OSC.

Meanwhile, the agency that initially had $984 million in lending authority, now has a pool of more than $210 billion due to domestic legislation signed by Trump in July 2025. Already in November 2025, the OSC announced a $620 million loan to Vulcan Elements, a company linked to Trump’s son, Donald Trump Jr.

Apparently, the murky Venezuelan energy deal is also Feinberg's brainchild.

👉 **The plunder of Venezuelan reserves continues**

But the Trump administration is seeking greater access to Venezuela’s mineral wealth, Reuters reports, citing sources familiar with the discussions.

The Trump administration is considering steps to expand US involvement in Venezuela’s mining sector, including gold, iron ore, bauxite, and nickel. One source said officials see critical minerals as a potential parallel track to the oil push. White House officials say existing laws provide a solid framework for investment, which suggests the possibility of a similar financial maneuver involving the Pentagon.

The Pentagon is openly becoming a[ US mercenary force](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73974), deposing governments and carrying out killings in exchange for a share of failed states’ wealth.

The US is already fuming that China has[ pulled ahead ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/56929)in the rare-earth mineral race, leaving the US far behind.

Those deposits could be potentially turned into drinking water, breathable air to sustain crews, or rocket fuel.
